title: The passive with ser: what happened to Tenochtitlan

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know the passive with *ser* + past participle from B1 Unit 18, and the passive with *se* from B1 Unit 6. A history of the conquest often puts the person or place that suffered the action first: *Tenochtitlan fue sitiada*. The participle agrees with that subject, and *por* can name who did it.

sections.title: Active and passive
rows: Active: Moctezuma, who acts, is the subject.
Passive: Cortés, who receives the action, is the subject; *por* names the doer.
Los españoles fueron expulsados de la ciudad.
Passive with no doer: the focus is on what happened to the Spaniards.

items.spanish: Cortés fue recibido en Tenochtitlan por Moctezuma.
items.english: Cortés was received in Tenochtitlan by Moctezuma.

items.spanish: Los españoles fueron expulsados de la ciudad durante la Noche Triste.
items.english: The Spaniards were expelled from the city during the Noche Triste.

items.spanish: La ciudad fue sitiada durante varios meses.
items.english: The city was besieged for several months.

items.spanish: Cuauhtémoc fue capturado el 13 de agosto de 1521.

sections.content: Use *fue* or *fueron* for a one-off event in the past, and make the participle agree: *la ciudad fue sitiada*, *los españoles fueron expulsados*. Leave out *por* when the doer is not important. Never use *era* for a single event with a date.
